statements.quote: American communities are rightfully questioning whether the rapid build-out of data centers
statements.context: Wyden was explaining his plan for a new excise tax on data centers and an end to certain tax breaks for them, citing local disruption and workers displaced by AI.

slowdown.note: No statement found for or against slowing frontier AI for safety reasons; his data center proposal is a tax, and the article reports (as a paraphrase) that he does not intend it to stop data center construction.

pause.note: No statement found for or against a pause on frontier AI development.

grade_reason: Seven searches and his official site turned up AI activity only on surveillance, privacy, data center taxes, state regulation and chip exports. No statement since 1 January 2025 acknowledging or dismissing catastrophic risk from AI was found.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. The search of his official site was incomplete: the site's own keyword filter did not work through the page fetcher (it returned the unfiltered archive), so only the newest page of press releases (20 October to 10 November 2026) was browsed directly. The one statement's quote is only the opening words of a longer sentence: the page-reading tool would not return more than about 125 characters, so I did not see the full sentence myself and the reviewer should open the article and either complete the quote or drop it. The tool described the rest as being about local disruption and workers displaced by AI. The statement date is the article date (6 August 2026); the article does not say how or exactly when the remark was made. The notus.org link redirects to https://washingtonsun.com/technology/democrats-split-ai-grows-wyden-tax-data-centers?redirected=notus_org, where the page was read. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (Sanders and Casar, September 2026): no source found showing Wyden as a co-sponsor; the Congress.gov co-sponsor list was not checked. China letter of 23 September 2026: not a signer, per the verified list. The Markey bill co-sponsorship and the chip export letter in the record come from search result summaries only and were not opened. The Anthropic-related letter (5 March 2026) is about government surveillance uses of AI and has no catastrophic risk content on the press release page.
